title: Tale of Aziz and Azizah
summary: While guiding Prince Taj al-Muluk on his quest, the faithful counselor Aziz wept as he recounted the tragic history of his youth and his cousin Azizah:
full_text:
While guiding Prince Taj al-Muluk on his quest, the faithful counselor Aziz wept as he recounted the tragic history of his youth and his cousin Azizah:

"In Damascus, my cousin Azizah and I were betrothed from our childhood. Her love for me was pure as morning dew, and her mind was gifted with the interpretation of poetry and omens. Yet in my youthful folly, I was easily distracted by every passing illusion.

One afternoon, as I walked through the perfumers’ souk, a mysterious lady dropped an embroidered handkerchief bearing the symbol of an open iris from an upper window. Captivated, I showed the handkerchief to Azizah. Instead of reproaching me with jealousy, my saintly cousin examined the cloth and interpreted the riddle: 'Cousin, she bids you meet her in two days at the hour of the second prayer.'

Time and again, Azizah used her superior wisdom to decipher the secret signs of my pursuit, guiding me away from perilous traps and preparing aromatic foods for my journeys, while her own heart broke in silence. She never spoke a word of anger, caring only for my well-being, though grief consumed her health day by day.

On the day of her passing, she placed a golden ring upon my finger and whispered her final counsel: 'When you meet with deceit, remember the words: Faithful love endures beyond the grave, while fickle passion vanishes like smoke.'

Only when she was laid to rest did the veil fall from my eyes. I realized that in pursuing fleeting shadows, I had neglected the truest, most angelic soul on earth. Stricken with remorse, I renounced worldly vanity and devoted my life to helping other travelers recognize the precious worth of sincere devotion before it is lost forever."
moral: Selfless devotion and unrequited fidelity are noble virtues, but one must never take true love for granted.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tale of Aziz and Azizah"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
